extracted.intended_audience: comic-book and graphic-novel creators, publishers, industry professionals, and fans (those interested in award nominations and winners)
extracted.subtask_description: Listing and announcing the Harvey Awards categories, nominees, winners, and Hall of Fame inductees—i.e., the award dimensions used to recognize outstanding achievement in comics and related media at New York Comic Con.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Book of the Year (category listed among the Harvey Awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes outstanding achievement in a comic/graphic book format. Examples of 2023 nominees listed on the page: Acting Class by Nick Drnaso; Ducks: Two Years in the Oil Sands by Kate Beaton; Follow Me Down: A Reckless Book by Ed Brubaker, Sean Phillips and Jacob Phillips; Girl Juice by Benji Nate; It's Lonely at the Centre of the Earth by Zoe Thorogood; Little Monsters Vol. 1 by Jeff Lemire & Dustin Nguyen; The Man in the McIntosh Suit by Rina Ayuyang; Mimosa by Archie Bongiovanni; Public Domain Vol. 1 by Chip Zdarsky; Who Will Make The Pancakes by Megan Kelso. (Page does not state explicit judging criteria beyond recognizing "outstanding achievement.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Book of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital Book of the Year (Harvey Awards category for works published digitally).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes outstanding achievement in digital comics/serialized web platforms. Example nominees on the page include Barnstormers by Scott Snyder and Tula Lotay (Comixology Originals); Deeply Dave by Grover; Everything is Fine by Mike Birchall (WEBTOON); Lore Olympus by Rachel Smythe (WEBTOON); Ripple Effects by Jordan Hart et al. Page frames this as a distinct award for digital-format works without detailed scoring rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Children’s or Young Adult Book (combined)
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Children’s or Young Adult Book (listed as a combined category in multiple years' announcements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes outstanding achievement for younger-reader-targeted comics and graphic novels. Example combined-category nominees include Clementine Fox and the Great Island Adventure by Leigh Luna; Dungeons & Dragons: Dungeon Club: Roll Call by Molly Knox Ostotag and Xanthe Bouma; Frizzy by Claribel A. Ortega and Rose Bousamra; Hungry Ghost by Victoria Ying; In Limbo: A Graphic Memoir by Deb JJ Lee; Northranger by Rey Terciero and Bre Indigo. Note: in some years the site lists Best Children’s Book and Best Young Adult Book as separate awards (see guidance entry below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Children’s Book (separate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Children’s Book (when listed separately in certain years' Harvey Awards announcements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When split from Young Adult, this category recognizes outstanding achievement specifically for children's comics/graphic novels. The page indicates that in some announcements (e.g., 2025) the Harvey Awards opened voting across separate Best Children’s Book and Best Young Adult Book categories, but the page does not provide separate nominee lists or specific selection criteria beyond the general purpose of honoring outstanding work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Young Adult Book (separate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Young Adult Book (when listed separately in certain years' Harvey Awards announcements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When split from Children’s, this category recognizes outstanding achievement specifically for YA-targeted comics/graphic novels. The site mentions both the combined and split arrangements across years; no explicit judging rubric is provided on-page beyond recognizing outstanding achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Manga
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Manga (Harvey Awards category recognizing manga works).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes outstanding achievement in manga. Example nominees shown include Cat + Gamer by Wataru Nadatani (translated by Zack Davisson); Chainsaw Man by Tatsuki Fujimoto (translated by Amanda Haley); Goodbye, Eri by Tatsuki Fujimoto (translated by Amanda Haley); Shuna's Journey by Hayao Miyazaki (translated by Alex Dudok de Wit); Spy x Family by Tatsuya Endo (translated by Casey Loe). The page lists translated works and publishers as examples; no scoring rubric is supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best International Book
rubrics_metrics.description: Best International Book (Harvey Awards category for works produced outside the U.S. or in translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes outstanding international comics/graphic novels (often translated). Example nominees: Alice on the Run: One Child's Journey Through the Rwandan Civil War by Gaspard Talmasse (translated by Nanette McGuinness); Always Never by Jordi Lafebre and Clemence Sapin (translated by Montana Kane); Ashes by Álvaro Ortiz (translated by Eva Ibarzabal); Blacksad: They All Fall Down Part 1 by Juan Díaz Canales and Juanjo Guarnido (translated by Diana Schutz and Brandon Kander); The Extraordinary Part: Book One: Orsay's Hands; Tiki: A Very Ruff Year. Page uses these examples but gives no explicit judging checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Adaptation from Comic Book/Graphic Novel
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Adaptation from Comic Book/Graphic Novel (category recognizing film/TV/games/other media adapted from comics or graphic novels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes outstanding adaptations of comic/graphic-novel source material into other media. Examples listed include American Born Chinese (Disney+), Drops of God (Apple TV+), Moon Knight (Disney+), Nimona (Netflix), The Sandman (Netflix), She-Hulk (Disney+), Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (feature film), The Stuff of Legend - The Board Game (board game adaptation), Sweet Tooth Season 2 (Netflix), Wednesday (Netflix). The page frames this as honoring adaptations but does not provide detailed evaluation criteria beyond being an adaptation of a comic/graphic-novel property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harvey Awards Hall of Fame Induction
rubrics_metrics.description: Harvey Awards Hall of Fame (annual inductees honored for significant contributions to comics and cartooning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes lifetime or historic contributions to the comics medium by creators and cartoonists. The page announces inductees and describes them as "Legendary Comic Book Creators and Cartoonists to be Honored"—examples of inductees across years include Wendy and Richard Pini (ElfQuest), Patrick McDonnell (Mutts), John Byrne, Peter David, Barbara Shermund, Akira Toriyama, Arthur Adams, Larry Hama, Sergio Aragonés, John Buscema, Rumiko Takahashi, Bernie Wrightson, Jeffrey Catherine Jones, Barry Windsor-Smith, Michael Kaluta. The page provides nomination/announcement context but does not list formal induction criteria or scoring mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: General award purpose: "recognizing outstanding achievement"
rubrics_metrics.description: The Harvey Awards are described on the page as "Recognizing outstanding achievement in multiple categories" and as one of the comic industry's oldest and most prestigious awards since 1988.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This phrase functions as the overarching evaluative standard for all categories on the site: winners and nominees are presented as exemplars of "outstanding achievement" in their respective category (book, digital, manga, international, adaptation, children/YA, Hall of Fame). No explicit scoring rubrics, judging panels, or point-based criteria are provided on the page; the standard is stated at a high level and illustrated by nominee/winner lists.
